accepted_contract: Use only the already selected standard GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 VM, retaining the 30-minute job timeout and dedicated per-job VM lifecycle as outer residual containment.

Normal owned-child cleanup must still be confirmed within the unchanged 20-second reserve. Every helper resource/time and scientific success gate remains unchanged, including the 600-second owned lifetime.

Uncertain pre-exec/spawn, uninterruptible OS or reap outcomes remain failed/incomplete with cleanup unconfirmed. The platform backstop cannot convert them into a successful 20-second cleanup or 600-second gate pass.
Do not claim an exact VM teardown timestamp, a custom process-group/cgroup guarantee, or verified termination of an unknown PID.
Keep the current minimal environments. No RUNNER_TRACKING_ID change, custom containment, installation or new permission is part of this clarification.

primary_sources.supports: GitHub provisions a VM for a hosted job and decommissions it after the job finishes.
Standard non-single-CPU GitHub-hosted runners are new VMs; single-CPU runners are a distinct shared-VM container case.
The job timeout triggers automatic cancellation. It does not state a precise physical teardown deadline.
Cancellation has staged signal/escalation handling and a service cancellation period. It is not an owned-child reap receipt.
The process-tracking environment key is RUNNER_TRACKING_ID.
The examined runner initializes a per-job marker and a pre-job process snapshot when process cleanup is enabled.
Final marker-based cleanup selects matching new processes, catches failures and has no explicit wait/reap confirmation in that loop.
The Linux marker lookup reads the target process environment; an omitted marker cannot match.
The examined Unix cancellation implementation targets its tracked process; its method name is not proof of an independently verified orphan-descendant cleanup.

runner_source_version_limit: Implementation references examine release v2.337.0, commit 397b032cbf865e9c3ddfab89d533ec19325e1273. They do not verify the version installed in any future job.

local_source_findings.provider: Pinned actions_policy requires github-hosted/Linux/X64/ubuntu-24.04/ubuntu24 and excludes job containers and namespace wrappers.
local_source_findings.workflow: The inherited WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE.yml.in specifies runs-on ubuntu-24.04 and timeout-minutes 30. The actual new workflow must separately retain and bind those values.
local_source_findings.owner_controller: OwnedSupervisor retains the first failure time and attempts known handles under its cleanup deadline. AttemptControl reports unresolved blocking/coordinator outcomes as incomplete and cleanup_confirmed=false.
local_source_findings.tracking_marker: The new helper environment contains LANG/LC_ALL only; inherited child_spec contains LANG/LC_ALL/TZ only. Neither forwards RUNNER_TRACKING_ID, so marker-based cleanup is excluded from this containment argument.
local_source_findings.child_guard: The reviewed child alarm/EOF guard begins once Python reaches the bootstrap body. It does not establish pre-exec or uninterruptible-kernel containment.

minimal_options.option: Retain current minimal child environments and explicitly rely only on the documented hosted-job/VM lifecycle as residual platform containment, while preserving strict owned success gates and cleanup-unknown failures.

A future separately reviewed narrow allowlist change could preserve the inherited tracking marker as an additional best-effort cleanup aid. It would still not prove the 20-second or 600-second gates and is not needed for the selected VM-lifecycle argument.

required_enabled_derivative_checks: Bind the exact standard hosted-runner/provider evidence and immutable workflow with the retained 30-minute timeout; do not substitute a self-hosted, single-CPU shared-container or custom runner.
Preserve cleanup_confirmed=false on every unknown outcome and keep normal success gates unchanged.
Review exact new claim/host/worker packet/dependency closure and source changes before activation; do not infer activation permission from this research.
